entries.author: Padmasambhava (quoted by Dudjom Rinpoche)
entries.quote: The truth of everything is the dharmakāya, which goes beyond the intellectual mind.
entries.edition: Rigpa Translations 2004; revised with permission, Lotsawa House 2026
entries.locator: Section 2, View; paragraph beginning “This rigpa, the indivisibility”
entries.context_note: Dudjom Rinpoche explicitly attributes this sentence to Guru Padmasambhava. It is a quotation within his exposition of appearance and emptiness, not independently verified against an earlier Padmasambhava text.
entries.rights: CC BY-NC 4.0

entries.author: Candrakīrti
entries.quote:
Conventional truth is the method;
And the ultimate is its outcome.
Not knowing how the two truths differ,
Your thoughts will wander astray.
entries.edition: Translation 2004; revised 2025; version 1.0–20250618
entries.context_note: Complete verse on distinguishing conventional and ultimate truth; translator’s primary bilingual selection, not an unattributed quotation aggregator.
entries.rights: CC BY-NC 4.0

entries.author: Uttamā (canonical attribution)
entries.quote: On the eighth, I stretched out my legs, having burst the mass of darkness.
entries.edition: Translation ©1997; Access to Insight BCBS edition, revised 4 August 2010
entries.context_note: Nun Uttamā describes attainment after instruction from a trustworthy nun and seven days of practice. “The eighth” refers to the eighth day, not an instantaneous guarantee.
entries.rights: CC BY-NC 4.0

entries.author: Seung Sahn
